questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How babies communicate before they can talk
How to help babies sleep at night
Why babies learn languages quickly
What parents should feed their babies
questions.why: They investigate how newborn babies tell their parents what's going on before they can speak.

questions.q: Why do Beth and Neil say they are hungry and ask for a pen at the start?
options: Because they forgot to eat and bring pens before the programme
To show that babies use the same words
To introduce a quiz about food
To show how easily adults can say what they want
questions.why: Beth says that as an adult she just opens her mouth and speaks, unlike babies.

questions.q: According to Beth, how can babies communicate?
options: Only by smiling
Only with their bodies or by crying
With simple words and signs
By copying their parents' faces
questions.why: She says babies can only communicate with their bodies or by crying.

questions.q: What does child psychotherapist Marie Derome say babies want us to know?
options: That they want to be left alone
That they understand everything we say to them from birth
That they depend on us completely to survive
That they need lots of toys
questions.why: She says they need us 'one hundred percent, because without us, they won't survive'.

questions.q: What does Marie say about babies' arm and leg movements?
options: They are completely random
Most of them are planned and have a purpose
They show that the baby is in pain
They only happen when babies are asleep or dreaming
questions.why: She says 75% of their movements are intentional and synchronised.

questions.q: What is the purpose of these movements, according to Marie?
options: To get their parents' attention and bring them closer
To make the muscles in their arms and legs grow stronger
To help them fall asleep
To show that they are hungry
questions.why: She says they're there 'to bring us in', saying 'Look at me. I need you.'

questions.q: What does Marie think about the idea of 'love at first sight' with a new baby?
options: It is true for almost all parents
It only happens with a first child
It is a lovely idea that all new parents should aim for
It is an unhelpful idea, because love takes time
questions.why: She calls it 'such an unhelpful cliché' and says it will take time to love the baby.

questions.q: Why, according to Neil, can this idea cause problems?
options: It makes new parents spend too much money on toys and clothes
It stops parents talking to doctors
It can create unrealistic hopes and make parents feel guilty
It makes babies cry more often
questions.why: He says it can create unrealistic expectations or make parents feel guilty.
